item.title: Swedish
item.description:
Technical Swedish

Living and working in Sweden one can go by a long way with using just English. However, now and then comes the time when you are asked to provide a summary of your talk/thesis/work/grant proposal in Swedish. The usual workflow is to write a good piece of text in English, run it via google translator or chatGPT, but then, human-intelligence is needed to handle odd translation of terms that are rarely (if ever) used in Swedish. For these terms IT-ord provides a good translation. Good luck!

item.title: Interview Questions
item.description: If you’re preparing for an interview (either as interviewee or interviewer), this is a good link to check out! It’s essentially a bot that returns common hiring questions for faculty appointments within computer science. Here you get a pdf with a good pool of questions for practicing.

item.title: About this website
item.description:
How did I build this website?

For academics, I think having a personal website is quite important as it allows you to quickly advertise news, collect and organize your work, and, most importantly, it is a great way for everyone around the world to know you exist and what you’re up to.

For several years I have used jekyll, but it started to get messy with the latest OS updates and gem versions. So for this website I’m using hugo, it does have a steep learning curve for beginners, but I’m really loving it ❤️
Here’s a quick comparison between hugo and jekyll.

item.title: 4 LaTeX
item.description:
Handy links for LaTeX

  • Detexify automatic recognition of handwritten symbols
  • latex-arrows visual list of latex commands for different types of arrows and more (e.g., very useful LaTeX for Beginners F.A.Q.)
  • latexpand to automatically combine all latex files into a single file. (If full latex is installed, you just need to type this command line: latexpand -empty-comments -o main_one_file.tex main.tex the long file output will appear in the Terminal)
  • mathcha for creating tikz pictures in a more eye-friendly way
  • FreeTikZ to transform handwritten diagrams into tikz
  • TikZiT GUI editor for graphs and string diagrams
  • CryptoBib the database that contains references to all iacr publications (remember to periodically download the latest version, which includes the most recent publications)
  • CryptoBib Search online tool for easy searching references in the crypto bib!
